title: Steer declaration
description: What a caller declares about how this run will be steered, carried in payload.steer of the one entry envelope (examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json) and validated with that example's own validator, so there is one validator and two documents. Every member is read at the point of decision in run.py. What a caller may NOT declare is as load-bearing as what it may: there is no member here that names a policy version, an engine, a rule, or a bundle, so a caller cannot pin, choose or soften the rules its own action will be judged by, and an entry that adds one is refused at 422 rather than honoured (F-b1-08). The decision engine and the containment class are configuration, not a caller's declaration.

surface.description: Where the decider works. stream: a subscription that shows the run in flight and carries the ask inline. parked-item: one queued item, request and response. Both are human-interaction adapters selected by this declaration; neither is named in the caller's line.

decision.description: What the decider does at the gate. approve, edit and reject are three of the four decisions the capability publishes; none means nobody decides, and the ask reaches its deadline. The fourth published decision, respond, is not exercised by this example.

decision_body.description: The reviewer's own body, checked against the ask's response schema before it is applied. On edit this is the artifact the run continues with - the agent proposes and the human publishes - so it is not a comment on the proposal.

decision_delay_seconds.description: How long the ask waits before the decision arrives, against the deadline the unit declares. Past the deadline the ask is terminal and a late decision is refused rather than applied.

intervention.description: The operator's verb on a cell whose turn did not finish. reconnect re-attaches to the unit the platform still holds; restart restores it from the checkpoint taken before the turn; replace clones its current state into a new unit. Each is a capability operation on the isolation adapter, decided by policy before it acts, and refused with a typed unsupported result where the containment class cannot serve it.

stall_first_turn.description: Run the first turn against an operation longer than the unit's wall ceiling, so the boundary ends it and there is a stuck cell for the operator to steer. The ceiling is enforced outside the unit either way.
